html:
In April 1993 Eritreans voted in a referendum observed by the United Nations, and 99.8 percent chose independence from Ethiopia, which was declared on 24 May 1993.

The vote followed the rebel victory in the war of independence two years earlier. The new Ethiopian government, led by former rebel allies, accepted the result, and Eritrea was admitted to the United Nations.

The new state left Ethiopia without a coast. Hopes of democracy faded: the constitution approved in 1997 was never put into force, and no national election has been held. Within five years the two countries were at war in the border war.
sum: In April 1993 Eritreans voted in a referendum observed by the United Nations, and 99.8 percent chose independence from Ethiopia, which was declared on 24 May 1993.
